A 19th-century academic oil painting with a smooth, finely blended surface: soft glazed transitions, delicate fine detail, minimal visible brushstrokes, no heavy impasto, no rough texture. Strong light and shadow from a single warm source (a lamp, a torch, a fire, a low sun) or from heavy overcast, with deep chiaroscuro. Palette of umber, ochre, gold, olive and near-black, with occasional cool accents. The manner of a romantic landscape, a grand historical scene, or a natural-history study of a creature painted as if real. A low, close viewpoint. Wet, reflective stone where there is stone; ancient architecture where there is architecture; one saturated subject held against darkness; scale shown by something small beside something vast. Quiet, watchful, ominous mood. No text, no lettering, no border, no frame, no grid texture, not photographic.

A close study of six old weights and an empty rack on a plank bench, in the dim hall of a long clay-walled, reed-roofed house, in the evening in early autumn, with the door shut and dark outside, seen from low at the height of the bench. A cloth is spread on the plank. On it, in a row from smallest to largest, lie six old weights: three of old bronze, dark and worn, and three of cut stone, the middle stone with an old chip at its foot. Beside them on the cloth stands a wooden rack cut with seven seats, all of them empty now, six dusty and the seventh, the largest, clean and bare. One small clay lamp burns on the bench beside the cloth and is the only light: it lights the bronze, the stone, the pale clean seat and the cloth gold, and leaves the room beyond in near-black. At the near edge of the bench, to one side, stands a tall, lean figure in a long coat with many deep pockets, the coat the first thing seen. The face is a middle-aged mortal's, plain, with steady eyes that watch as a man watches a scale while the pans settle. The hands are stained with ink and green verdigris. A pair of small, plain brass scales, slightly dented, hangs at the belt. Seen from behind or in deep shadow, the head turned away or lost in darkness, no face visible. Here the figure stands still with its stained hands at its sides, turned toward the weights. Across the cloth, at the far edge of the lamplight, a grey-haired man with thick potter's fingers stands as a dark shape, his face lost in shadow, the lamp catching only his hair and one hand resting on the plank. At the end of the bench a wooden weighing beam hangs on a cord with two shallow pans of fired clay. By the clay wall, almost in darkness, a reed basket holds a nest of small unmarked fired clay pieces. No other figures. No metal armor, no stone walls, no windows. The small bright row of weights and the one clean empty seat, beside the tall dark figure and the black depth of the hall, give the scale.
